title: Connect native browser Case selection to existing independently authorized Inspector row
goal: Allow a Case Analyst to select a currently visible Case in the opt-in Case Queue browser, reauthorize it through the existing first-party inspect_case endpoint on the exact current filtered/paged projection, display a minimal read-only selection summary and restore source focus without cloning Shared Inspector or granting Workspace permissions.
invariants: Each visual selection rechecks the current authenticated host via GET /case-queue?inspect_case=EXACT_ID including current q/limit/cursor; no client-side ACL or alternate owner.
Server first-party Case/Incident/Finding ACL determines selection; rejected/mismatched response displays no previously selected data, no partial Case preview.
Only inert textContent of a bounded subset of the newly authorized Case row is displayed. No raw Incident/Finding/source preview, bearer, policy or tenant-selection control.
Changing search/page, denial, or pagehide invalidates in-flight selections; close/Escape returns focus to the original current row when still present.
This is a read-only selection context not the canonical Shared Inspector visual component, Case Workspace route, assignment, export, Saved View editing or production IAM.
security_properties: A successful list row is not authority for Inspector; perform a separate server reauthorization with exact opaque ID and current cursor/filter.
Reject a returned Inspector row with a different Case ID or invalid shape; never display metadata from an unauthorized response.
Clear selection on page/filter changes, deny/error and pagehide, including pending requests, without retaining source details.
Client never accepts a tenant/environment/permission selector or stores a bearer token.

migration.rationale: Opt-in same-origin host-mounted static browser with no changed persistence or Case schema

rollback.strategy: Stop using NewAuthorizedQueueBrowserHandler and use existing native authorized Queue HTTP handler
verification: Existing GET Case Queue and POST return routes remain available
No data persisted in browser or backend

inputs: Existing native first-party GET inspect_case Class-0 projection in PR #147 and opt-in Queue browser from PR #148; both owner-authorized, parent R is NOT main.
Canonical CAP-INV-101 §17, Shared Inspector anatomy and keyboard contract; Shared owns final reusable Inspector UI and host owns current IAM/session.
outputs: A per-row read-only Inspect action using current query/page and exact Case ID, current reauthorized first-party Case response, minimal accessible text summary.
Closing selection with button or Escape returns keyboard focus without clearing Queue search/page; filtering, paging, denial or navigation purges selection.
acceptance_tests: Node DOM tests: exact opaque Case with significant spaces is sent unchanged, freshly authorized response displayed with inert textContent and keyboard focus restored.
Node tests: server-denied inspection or response with different Case ID does not show previous selection; page navigation purges selection and responses.
Existing Go owner HTTP tests cover source-specific revocation, current page cursor and per-object ACL; no new backend provider or external dependency.
Exact-head engineering-kernel includes required CHK-MANIFESTS, CHK-CASE-QUEUE-CONTRACT, CHK-SECURITY-TESTS without threshold waiver.

performance_budget.rationale: Only explicit per-row user action causes one additional first-party owner-authorized request; no background polling; same bounded 25-row page and candidate limit.
metrics: 0 extra requests during normal pagination until click

definition_of_ready: Parent Q browser and P native inspect_case handler are already implemented on immutable HEAD; no Shared Inspector final UI is claimed.
Single reader principal's browser is authenticated by current host cookie/session and server ACL, not by selected Case ID.
definition_of_done: Published new bounded task and code on child of PR #148; exact CI/commits documented; one independent L2 when material and verifiable.
No native merge pending ancestors and no full CAP-INV-101 product acceptance claimed.
